videos.title: US to Issue Visas to Flavio Bolsonaro and His Family
videos.description:
"Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Michael Oren, former Israeli ambassador to the US, says many Israelis are in shock as Gadi Eisenkot's bloc holds a narrow lead over Benjamin Netanyahu's, but cautions that the result could still change as votes are counted. Rep. Greg Landsman (D-OH) says more voters are casting ballots early and that the numbers suggest a strong night for Democrats in Ohio, while cautioning there are still seven days until Election Day. Rep. Darrell Issa (R-CA) says redistricting could backfire in some states by creating more competitive seats that require significant campaign spending.

videos.title: Rep. Issa Says Redistricting Creates More Seats in Play
videos.description:
Rep. Darrell Issa (R-CA) says redistricting could backfire in some states by creating more competitive seats that require significant campaign spending. Issa says Flavio Bolsonaro's departure from Brazil could help settle questions around the country's transition of power, while cautioning that his presence in the US does not necessarily mean he will be allowed to conduct political activity from here. On Israel, Issa says Netanyahu would likely continue an aggressive approach toward Iran, Gaza and southern Lebanon if he remains prime minister during another election cycle. Issa also says Congress should address the debt ceiling during the lame-duck session and expects lawmakers to pass the defense authorization bill on a broadly bipartisan basis. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power."

videos.title: Oren Says Netanyahu Could Benefit From Another Election
videos.description:
Michael Oren, former Israeli ambassador to the US, says many Israelis are in shock as Gadi Eisenkot's bloc holds a narrow lead over Benjamin Netanyahu's, but cautions that the result could still change as votes are counted. Oren says that if Eisenkot cannot assemble the 61 seats needed to form a government, Israel could face another election while Netanyahu remains prime minister. He says time is working in Netanyahu's favor. Oren says a new prime minister could get a grace period in Washington, but adds that Israel's core security policies would be unlikely to change substantially. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power."

videos.title: Traders Brace for Fed Day
videos.description:
The Federal Reserve kicked off a two-day meeting Tuesday after raising interest rates after its previous meeting in September. Bloomberg News Federal Reserve and Economy Reporter Enda Curran says the meeting comes amid the "most confusing economy yet." Meanwhile, Israel voters are heading to the polls for the first national election since the October 7th attack. Bloomberg News Israel Bureau Chief Ethan Bronner breaks down what's at stake. Then, CEO at Harrison Street Asset Management Chris Merrill talks impacts of inflation of alternative real estate investing. Plus, Olympic Marathon Champion and longtime Nike Partner Eliud Kipchoge discusses his running 'World Tour' and how he has worked with Nike over decades to evolve racing gear and push the sport forward.

videos.title: GM to Leave NYSE for Stock Listing on Tech-Focused Nasdaq
videos.description:
General Motors plans to shift its stock listing to the Nasdaq Global Select Market from the New York Stock Exchange to position the company as a tech-forward company. The company will retain the “GM” ticker symbol when it begins trading on the Nasdaq on Nov. 17, and the new listing offers eligibility for potential inclusion in the Nasdaq-100 Index. Bloomberg's David Welch joins to discuss.
